By assuming Gaussian skill θ* and linearizing the loss around it, they derive a closed-form expression for the expected skill trajectory E[θ_k], mean squared deviation d̄_k, and mean loss l̄_k. This allows derivation of β_{o,k} = v / tr(R)/M, where R encodes the schedule structure. The convergence time constant τ1 emerges from the spectral radius of the update matrix, and the hard bound β < 2v ensures numerical stability. These primitives enable GSE to dynamically tune K-factors and GSI to perform Bayesian inference on skill distributions with bounded uncertainty.
